rules.rationale: ESOL evidence: long SMILES lowered solubility (-11.46). LogD is inverse of solubility, so large scaffolds should raise lipophilicity.
Source prior: short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89); small compact molecules are typically hydrophilic and low logD.
Ring role carried the strongest transfer weight (0.758); ring-rich carbon surface reduces solvation and increases partitioning.
Donor-to-heteroatom role mapping implies polar contacts; hydrogen bonding capacity lowers octanol-water partition coefficients.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size and ring effects with sign inversion, assuming lipophilicity is anti-correlated with aqueous solubility. Fails if the target pool's large molecules are polar or ionizable, breaking the inversion.

rules.rationale: Halogens add polarizable nonpolar surface with weak hydration; classic strong positive contribution to logP/logD.
Unhalogenated majority lacks that hydrophobic substituent boost, giving a mechanistically interpretable low-lipophilicity baseline.
Extended aromatic pi systems bury nonpolar surface, favoring octanol phase over water.
Counter-hypothesis: the low-confidence (0.22) length role may not invert; very long molecules are often polar, multi-functional.

skills.hypothesis: Substituent-level domain knowledge (halogen, aromatic surface) drives lipophilicity while explicitly downweighting the uncertain size transfer. Fails if halogen_high coverage (98) is too sparse to inform the surrogate early.

fixed_initial.lesson: Cross-assay transfer from ESOL to lipophilicity requires sign inversion, not direct reuse; the highest-transfer-weight roles (ring, branch) and broad-coverage bins give more usable surrogate features than rare halogen bins.
fixed_initial.revision_summary: Kept the mechanistically strongest source-grounded skill by inverting ESOL solubility effects for size and ring roles, and paired it with a domain-knowledge halogen/aromatic counter-hypothesis that downweights the low-confidence (0.22) length transfer. All conditions use exact catalog field-value pairs; deployment frozen on the inversion skill for broader pool coverage.

rules.rationale: Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758, effect 9.94); fused ring carbon adds poorly hydrated nonpolar surface.
Donor-to-heteroatom role maps hydrogen bonding capacity; polar contacts retain water solvation and lower logD.
Rotatable-bond role (weight 0.758): flexible branching exposes polar groups and costs conformational entropy on octanol transfer.
Heteroatom-sparse scaffolds approach pure hydrocarbon, the classic high-logP extreme of drug-like chemical space.

skills.hypothesis: Retains the higher-scoring generation-1 skill built on the two strongest transfer roles (ring and branch, weight 0.758) plus heteroatom polarity; fails if ring-rich molecules here are heavily oxygenated or ionizable.

rules.rationale: Extended aromatic pi surface is poorly hydrated and strongly favors the octanol phase, raising partition coefficients.
Aliphatic, aromatic-poor scaffolds in this pool tend to be polar aliphatic chains with lower octanol-water partitioning.
Counter-hypothesis: the length role is the least confident transfer (0.22); size effect is retained only weakly, not as a driver.
Halogen substituents add polarizable, weakly hydrated surface; the mid bin (743 molecules) gives usable coverage unlike halogen_high.

skills.hypothesis: Domain-knowledge aromatic and halogen substituent surface drives lipophilicity while explicitly downweighting the uncertain size transfer; fails if aromatic_high molecules in this pool carry dominant polar heterocycles.

true_feedback.lesson: Across two generations the ring/branch/heteroatom skill scored 89.3 mean AUC versus 88.0 for the length-inversion skill, and the earlier generation showed the same ordering direction, but both gaps sit inside the 83-93 per-seed spread, so the ordering is suggestive rather than established. The consistent signal is that broad-coverage bins grounded in the highest transfer weights (ring and branch, 0.758) behave at least as well as the low-confidence length role (0.22), which never separated from noise.
true_feedback.revision_summary: Promoted the previously non-deployed flexible_ring_balance_partition core to deployment as ring_branch_polarity_partition, since it led on development AUC in generation 1 and rests on the two highest transfer-weight roles with broad bin coverage; the branch penalty was softened slightly to reduce over-shrinkage of a 1183-molecule bin. The counter-hypothesis skill now demotes the low-confidence length role to a near-zero weight instead of using it as a driver, and replaces the sparse halogen_high bin (98 candidates) with halogen_mid (743) so the substituent feature can actually inform the surrogate. Deployment frozen on ring_branch_polarity_partition.

rules.rationale: ESOL long SMILES cut solubility (-11.46); bulky carbon scaffolds resist hydration and favor octanol.
Source prior: short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89); small polar molecules partition weakly into octanol.
Ring role carried top transfer weight (0.758); fused ring carbon surface disfavors aqueous solvation.
Donor-to-heteroatom mapping implies polarity; few heteroatoms means hydrocarbon-like character and higher logD.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size, ring, and polarity roles with sign inversion, assuming solubility and lipophilicity anti-correlate. Fails if large pool molecules are polar or ionizable, breaking the inversion.

rules.rationale: Halogen substitution adds polarizable, poorly hydrated surface; the mid bin gives usable coverage (743) for the surrogate.
The unhalogenated majority lacks that hydrophobic substituent boost, a mechanistic low-logD baseline.
Extended aromatic pi systems bury nonpolar surface area, favoring the octanol phase over water.
Counter-hypothesis: low-confidence (0.22) length role may not invert; very long molecules are often multifunctional and polar.

skills.hypothesis: Substituent-level domain knowledge drives lipophilicity while reversing the uncertain size transfer at extreme length. Fails if halogenation in this pool co-occurs with strongly polar or ionizable groups.

no_feedback.lesson: ESOL-to-lipophilicity transfer requires sign inversion, and rules should sit on well-covered bins with contrast: the high-transfer ring role plus long/short length priors and the sparse hetero_low bin discriminate better than a 63%-coverage hetero_high rule.
no_feedback.revision_summary: Rewrote both skills with schema-correct single field-value condition objects. The source-grounded inversion skill now uses hetero_low as a positive hydrocarbon marker instead of a broad hetero_high penalty and lifts the short-SMILES penalty, keeping the high-transfer ring role. The counter-hypothesis skill shifts from the sparse halogen_high bin (98) to halogen_mid (743) for learnable coverage while retaining the very_long downweight of the low-confidence length role. Deployment is frozen on the inversion skill for broader pool coverage and stronger source grounding.

rules.rationale: Fused aromatic ring systems bury large rigid nonpolar surface, the dominant positive term in octanol-water partitioning.
Extended pi surface resists hydration; broad coverage (1982) makes this a well-conditioned surrogate feature.
Fully aliphatic solutes in this pool are typically small and polar, giving low partition coefficients.
Branch role carried high transfer weight (0.758); alkyl branching adds hydrophobic bulk and shields polar centers.

skills.hypothesis: High-coverage aromatic and branch descriptors, sharpened by a fused aromatic-ring interaction, drive lipophilicity. Fails if aromatic bulk here co-occurs with ionizable or strongly polar substituents that suppress logD.

rules.rationale: Few heteroatoms means little hydrogen bonding and low desolvation cost, favoring the octanol phase.
Dense heteroatoms give polar contacts and hydration, lowering octanol-water partitioning.
Halogen substituents add polarizable, weakly hydrated surface; halogen_mid (743) has usable coverage unlike halogen_high.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence (0.22) inverted length transfer; long scaffolds often carry many polar groups.

skills.hypothesis: Polarity content, not molecular size, sets lipophilicity; the inverted ESOL length relation is explicitly reversed. Fails if hetero_low (194) is too sparse to anchor the surrogate early.

shuffled_feedback.lesson: Across two development generations the aromatic/branch skill matched or beat the ESOL length-inversion skill on both mean AUC and mean final best, so broad-coverage surface descriptors are the safer deployment; sparse bins remain weak surrogate features.
shuffled_feedback.revision_summary: Promoted the aromatic/branch family to deployment and sharpened it with a fused aromatic-ring interaction while dropping the redundant very-long-length rule. Built the counter-hypothesis around heteroatom polarity and moderate halogenation, explicitly reversing the low-confidence inverted length transfer rather than repeating it. Semantic mass still decays toward the target-only anchor; all conditions map exact catalog fields to exact catalog values, and no target outcomes were used.
